name: Problem-Solution Fit Scorecarding
phase: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
hypothesis: We believe our proposed solution addresses the primary pain points discovered in Phase 1. We will verify this by scoring our feature set against validated customer problems using a blind scoring rubric, and consider it validated if ≥ 80% of features map directly to high-severity problems, with all secondary unmapped features eliminated.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: List validated customer problems on the vertical axis and proposed feature specifications across the top.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: For each intersection ask whether the feature relieves that problem, and justify it with phase-one data.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Compute the coverage ratio; drop features that solve unvalidated problems or miss the core bottleneck.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Construct a matrix listing validated customer problems on the vertical axis and proposed feature specifications on the horizontal axis.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Evaluate each intersection: Does this feature directly alleviate this specific problem? Require cross-functional leads to justify each connection with behavioral data gathered in Phase 1.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Calculate the operational coverage ratio. Flag and discard features that solve unvalidated problems or fail to resolve the core bottleneck.

warning.label: Sunk Cost Feature Attachment
warning.text: Teams write elaborate post-hoc justifications for favourite features with no link to validated problems.

warningFull: Product teams routinely construct elaborate post-hoc justifications for favorite features that have no demonstrable link to validated customer problems.
